Lexicon Latīnitātis Cotīdiānae
Aa

Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

pour out verb

also dump, tip out, empty out

classical

Liv. 23.12.1: effundī … jussit ānulōs aureōs
Petr. 135.2: partem legūminis super mēnsam effūdit

effundō, effundere

verb, third conjugation

Of solid things too, tipped out of a container: rings, beans, sand.

Other words

  • diffundō, diffundere, diffūdī, diffūsum — spread by pouring, pour out; spread, scatter

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Verg. A. 1.319: dederatque comam diffundere ventīs (Lewis & Short); Ov. Met. 1.36 (Lewis & Short)

  • profundō, profundere, profūdī, profūsum — pour out or forth, shed freely; lavish, squander

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Clu. 18: sanguinem suum profundere omnem cupit (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • Harēnam effunde.

    Pour out the sand.composed

  • effundī in vestibulō cūriae jussit ānulōs aureōs

    he had the gold rings tipped out in the entrance of the senate houseLiv. 23.12.1

  • partem legūminis super mēnsam effūdit jussitque mē dīligenter pūrgāre

    she tipped some of the beans out on the table and told me to pick them over carefullyPetr. 135.2

  • dederatque comam diffundere ventīs

    and she had given her hair to the winds to spreadVerg. A. 1.319 (Lewis & Short)

  • sanguinem suum profundere omnem cupit

    she is eager to pour out all her own bloodCic. Clu. 18 (Lewis & Short)

See also empty, fill, dump truck, dump.
